title: Mock 2: solvers, OR-Tools and the search

questions.heading: Round 1: The Search Brackets the Optimum Between Two Numbers
questions.stem: HiGHS, at its default tolerances, ends a maximization with status OPTIMAL, a plan worth $24,260k and a best bound of $24,262k. What does that tell you?

options.text: That no plan is worth more than $24,260k, since OPTIMAL is a proof
options.says: OPTIMAL means optimal within the run's tolerances; the bound says a plan worth up to $24,262k may exist.

options.text: That the bound is wrong by $2k, since an optimal run closes the gap
options.says: The bound is a value no plan can beat; a gap stop leaves it above the incumbent, and that is not an error.

options.text: That no plan beats $24,260k by more than $2k, within the tolerance
options.says: Right: the optimum lies between the incumbent and the bound, and the run stopped because they were close enough.

options.text: That the plan is unique, since an optimal run stops at one best plan
options.says: Plans within the gap can pick different projects; one solve says nothing about uniqueness.

questions.heading: Trap Questions: Claims About the API That Do Not Hold
questions.stem: A minimization stops with a plan costing 1,000 and a best bound of 800. Which relative gaps do HiGHS and SCIP report?

options.text: HiGHS 20%, dividing by the plan; SCIP 25%, dividing by the bound
options.says: Right: HiGHS divides the 200 by the incumbent, SCIP by the smaller of the two numbers in size, here the bound.

options.text: HiGHS 25%, dividing by the bound; SCIP 20%, dividing by the plan
options.says: The other way round: HiGHS divides by the incumbent, SCIP by the smaller number.

options.text: Both 20%, since each solver divides the gap by the incumbent
options.says: Only HiGHS divides by the incumbent; SCIP divides by the smaller number, the 800.

options.text: Both 25%, since each solver divides the gap by the best bound
options.says: HiGHS divides by the incumbent, so its gap is 20%.

questions.heading: Trap Questions: Claims About the API That Do Not Hold
questions.stem: You guard 12 planning rules with flags, add the flags as assumptions and solve with CP-SAT on one worker. The model is infeasible, and the solver names 9 flags. What do you report to the planners?

options.text: The 9 as the minimal conflict, since the solver names the fewest flags
options.says: The named set is sufficient for the conflict, not promised minimal; lesson 4.6.2 got 28 back where 3 were enough.

options.text: Nothing yet, since the call returns rule names just for a minimal set
options.says: The call returns variable indices, which you map to rule names, minimal or not.

options.text: The 12 as the conflict, since each assumed flag takes part in it
options.says: The solver named 9 of the 12; the printed example named 3 of 5.

options.text: The flags left after a deletion filter, as the 9 may not be minimal
options.says: Right: check the named set with a deletion filter before calling it minimal.
